physicalNotes: Radius 0.09206903 Jupiter radii from Greklek-McKeon et al. 2025 (2025AJ....170...65G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170...65G/abstract): 6,582.2 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.00286318 Jupiter masses (Greklek-McKeon et al. 2025, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2025AJ....170...65G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170...65G/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Peterson et al. 2023 (2023Natur.617..701P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PETERSON_ET_AL_2023): P 2.753436 d
sources.shape: Greklek-McKeon et al. 2025 (2025AJ....170...65G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname GREKLEK_MCKEON_ET_AL_2025): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.01992 au and stellar radius 0.182 solar radii; Greklek-McKeon et al. 2025 (2025AJ....170...65G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname GREKLEK_MCKEON_ET_AL_2025): inclination 89.34 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Peterson et al. 2023 (2023Natur.617..701P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PETERSON_ET_AL_2023): transit mid-time 2458772.16211 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 15 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
